target_customer: Parents of young children who want to share printed photos with family
problem: Families take many photos but rarely print and mail them, so grandparents and relatives miss them.
business_model: pay per print, automated printing and mailing of selected photos

founders.name: Paul Stamatiou
founders.background_notes: Joined Twitter as Experience Designer in January 2013 and stayed as advisor (TechCrunch, 2013-01). Later head of design at Sesame per the YC page.

founders.name: Akshay Dodeja
founders.background_notes: Recruited by Stamatiou after Paul Graham suggested ideas (tech.co). Later founder of Terminal 49 per the YC page.

exit.reason: In January 2013 the founders said it was not shutting down and they sought a new team; CB Insights later lists it as ceased operations without a date.

competitors.name: Postagram (Sincerely)
competitors.what: Mobile app that prints Instagram photos as postcards and mails them

technical_complexity.rationale: Photo selection, ordering and handing printing to a fulfillment partner; the founders said the service was nearly fully automated by 2013.

defensibility.rationale: Large printers such as Shutterfly and Snapfish could offer the same, and the product relied on commodity printing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in January 2013 called Snapfish a photo printing powerhouse and noted Shutterfly's acquisitions of photo startups; no source says they copied Picplum.

market_need_then: Mobile photo volume was growing in 2011 and Demo Day pitched busy new parents; no demand figures were found.

branding.name_origin: TechCrunch (January 2013) says the name reflects encouraging users to pick only the best, high quality photos for printing.
branding.domain_note: Used picplum.com (YC page); it now redirects to an unrelated site.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.visual_style: Design led, with a designer co-founder
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, family oriented, as 'the hassle-free way to share your best moments'.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, The Next Web and Xconomy in 2011 and 2012; no merch or fan base found.

brand_strength.rationale: Pleasant name and design pedigree with launch press, but confusable with the similar Picplz and no lasting recognition.

outcome_analysis: Picplum automated printed photo delivery for families and launched through YC in 2011 with a tiny reported seed. By January 2013 one co-founder joined Twitter and the other moved to Live Nation Labs, leaving the product running in spare time with revenue but without a team, and the founders had taken personal offers instead of selling the company. Strong incumbents and a part time team kept it from scaling; the final shutdown date is not public.
notes: The $20K seed rests on CB Insights alone. A 2012 Xconomy piece, as quoted in a search summary, says the 2011 seed came from Y Combinator, Start Fund and 500 Startups; I could not confirm the other two, so only Y Combinator is listed. The YC page does not give a shutdown and CB Insights shows no date. The failure factors are a judgment from the January 2013 article, which does not state a cause of failure. TechCrunch 2013 says Picplum debuted in summer 2010 while the YC batch is Summer 2011 and the 2011 coverage fits that; the discrepancy is unresolved. picplum.com now redirects to an unrelated site.
